ops.text: ; and (i) the exclusive right, for itself and its licensees, lessees and their financing parties, to use the roof, exterior walls, electrical rooms, parking areas and other portions of the Project outside the Demised Premises for solar and other energy generation, energy storage, electric-vehicle charging, telecommunications and related equipment, and to install, operate, maintain, replace and remove such equipment and the conduit, wiring and connections serving it, including through the Demised Premises in locations that do not materially reduce Tenant’s usable floor area.  All revenue, credits, incentives and environmental attributes from the equipment described in clause (i) belong to Landlord or its licensees.  In exercising its rights under clause (i), Landlord shall use commercially reasonable efforts to minimize interference with Tenant’s business, and such work shall not be an eviction or entitle Tenant to any abatement of rent.  Landlord shall give Tenant at least twenty-four (24) hours’ notice of any planned interruption of electrical service for work under clause (c) (except in an emergency or where the utility gives less notice), shall schedule it outside Tenant’s normal business hours where the utility permits, and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to limit its duration. ops.label: P5 §10(d)
ops.anchor_text: Should any of the Building equipment or machinery cease to function properly

runs.text: Utility Data

.  Within ten (10) days after Landlord’s request, Tenant shall deliver, or sign the utility’s authorization allowing Landlord to obtain directly, Tenant’s electricity and gas consumption and billing data (including interval data, where available) for the Demised Premises for the prior twenty-four (24) months and for the remainder of the Lease Term.  Landlord may use such data for building benchmarking, regulatory compliance, energy and capacity planning and incentive applications, and shall not disclose Tenant-identifiable data except as required by law or to its lenders, consultants and energy providers under a duty of confidentiality.

ops.label: P3 §10(c)
ops.anchor_text: Should any of the Building equipment or machinery cease to function properly

runs.text: Electrical Capacity

.  Tenant’s electrical service is limited to the service serving the Demised Premises on the Commencement Date.  Tenant shall not apply to any utility for new, additional or upgraded service, or for interconnection of any generation or storage, without Landlord’s prior written consent, which Landlord may withhold in its sole discretion.  Any electrical capacity, service, transformer, switchgear or metering added to the Project, by whomever paid for, is part of the Project, shall remain at the end of the Lease Term, and Landlord may allocate it among the Project’s occupants.  Tenant shall not remove any electrical service equipment, notwithstanding any right to remove its trade fixtures.

ops.label: P8 §36 sub "Insurance, Indemnity and Removal"
ops.anchor_text: Tenant warrants that all such financial information heretofore

runs.text: Insurance, Indemnity and Removal

.  Tenant shall insure the Backup Power Equipment under its property insurance and carry any additional liability or pollution coverage Landlord reasonably requires, naming the additional insureds required by the section of this Lease entitled “INSURANCE”, and Tenant’s indemnity in the section of this Lease entitled “INDEMNITY” applies to all claims arising from the Backup Power Equipment.  When this Lease ends, Tenant shall remove the Backup Power Equipment and all fuel and batteries and repair all resulting damage, except that Landlord may elect by notice to keep any conduit, wiring, pads and switchgear, which then become Landlord’s property without payment.

ops.label: P8 §36 sub "Fuel and Battery Materials"
ops.anchor_text: Tenant warrants that all such financial information heretofore

runs.text: Fuel and Battery Materials

.  Notwithstanding the section of this Lease entitled “ENVIRONMENTAL MATTERS”, Tenant may keep in the Backup Power Equipment the fuel and battery chemistry Landlord approves under this section, in the approved quantities (“
Approved Backup Materials

”); all other Hazardous Materials remain prohibited.  Approved Backup Materials remain Hazardous Materials for purposes of Tenant’s cleanup and indemnity obligations, which apply to them in full, and Tenant shall report any spill, leak, fire or thermal event to Landlord immediately.

ops.label: P8 §36 sub "Location, Fuel and Operation"
ops.anchor_text: Tenant warrants that all such financial information heretofore

runs.text: Location, Fuel and Operation

.  The location, fuel type and maximum quantity of fuel stored on the Project are limited to those Landlord approves in advance.  Tenant shall test the Backup Power Equipment only at times Landlord reasonably approves, keep its exhaust, noise and vibration within the limits Landlord reasonably sets and the law allows, and, except during a utility outage, stop operating it on Landlord’s notice that it is disturbing other occupants or damaging the Building until the condition is corrected.

ops.label: P8 §36 sub "Electrical Connection"
ops.anchor_text: Tenant warrants that all such financial information heretofore

runs.text: Electrical Connection

.  The Backup Power Equipment shall serve only the Demised Premises and shall connect to the Demised Premises’ electrical system only through a listed transfer switch that prevents any back-feed to the utility, the Building’s electrical system or any other occupant.  Tenant shall not interconnect the Backup Power Equipment with the utility grid, export power from it, or apply to any utility in connection with it, without Landlord’s prior written consent under the section of this Lease entitled “SERVICES AND UTILITIES”.

ops.label: P8 §36 sub "Approvals and Codes"
ops.anchor_text: Tenant warrants that all such financial information heretofore

runs.text: Approvals and Codes

.  Before ordering or installing the Backup Power Equipment, Tenant shall deliver its specifications, location, fuel type and on-site fuel quantity, single-line electrical diagram and installer’s written scope, and shall not proceed until Landlord approves them in writing; Landlord may have them reviewed by an engineer of its choice at Tenant’s cost.  Any generator shall be installed, tested and maintained in accordance with NFPA 37 and NFPA 110, and any battery energy storage system shall be listed to UL 9540, supported by UL 9540A test data, and installed in accordance with NFPA 855 and the local fire code.  All work shall be done at Tenant’s cost by licensed contractors approved by Landlord, under all required governmental permits, and in accordance with the section of this Lease entitled “ALTERATIONS”.
